quarterly_data.signal: IP REACHES A $1 BILLION RUN RATE THIS YEAR ON ADVANCED-NODE CONNECTIVITY TITLES: Head of IR Richard Gu said the deliberately narrow advanced-node IP strategy - 'Be it HBM, UCI, PCI, all these connectivity kind of important icon IP' exposed to the AI super cycle - means 'in share in the market, we're going to be at a $1 billion clip by the end of the year', with IP 'growing north of 40%' in Q2, 'At scale and growing much faster than market.' He credited a widening foundry ecosystem: 'Now it is not just TSMC, it is Intel, it is Samsung, it is Rapidus. We are working with them all', while holding company incremental margin at 50%.
quarterly_data.figure: IP at a $1 billion clip by the end of the year; IP growing north of 40%; 50% incremental margin

quarterly_data.signal: HOW THE SUPER AGENTS ARE PRICED - THREE MONETIZATION VECTORS: Gu said Cadence is 'creating separate price books for these four super agents, and in terms of the pricing, it is all going to be commensurate to what a human designer's skills could be. It will be worth tens of thousands of dollars.' Second, 'Once the customer exceeds or surpass the prescribed workload within that super agent... we want to charge them additional consumption in terms of tokens and extra usage.' Third is pull-through of the underlying tools, because agents 'do not need like 80 hours sleep' and explore far more broadly than a human designer, making the model 'a lot more pay-as-to-usage.' He cited Jensen Huang at Computex saying ChipStack is delivering a 40X productivity benefit.
quarterly_data.figure: super-agent price books worth tens of thousands of dollars each; ChipStack cited at 40X productivity

quarterly_data.signal: THE TAM MATH FOR AGENTIC EDA - TOOLS COULD GO FROM ~10% TO ~33% OF CUSTOMER R&D: Gu said EDA spend inside a customer's design R&D budget 'is still like low teens, call it 10%, 11%. The massive 90% of the spend is still in human designers.' Against a workload increase of '30, 40x' over the next five to six years that no company can hire against, 'There are customers of ours telling us they are willing to spend more than 50% of what we spend on a human being, human designer, on automation tokens and chip designs... it is almost like 33% of the R&D budget.'
quarterly_data.figure: EDA at 10%, 11% of design R&D today vs 90% human designers; customers willing to spend more than 50% of a human designer's cost on automation tokens, almost 33% of the R&D budget; 30, 40x workload increase

quarterly_data.signal: CHINA GUIDED TO GROW AT LEAST AT THE COMPANY AVERAGE IN 2026: Gu said 'we're also pretty confident that China is going to grow at least at a company average this year', that Q2 China strength reflects bookings and add-on deals from the past couple of quarters, and that the demand mirrors the US - 'They have great LLM model companies. They have good hyperscalers, a lot of EV kind of autonomous driving vehicle companies.' On local competitors he said they remain point-tool players without a full flow and, importantly, without 'the foundry ecosystem or certification from TSMC', so they are 'not a near-term or medium-term threat.'
quarterly_data.figure: China guided to grow at least at the company average this year

connects_to.relationship: Millennium simulation supercomputer built on NVIDIA GPUs

contracts.signal: Gu described Millennium as the three-layer cake applied to simulation - 'In the bottom layer is the GPU from NVIDIA... in the middle layer is all these principled software in simulation' - launched 'about a year and a half, 2 years ago, together with NVIDIA.' He said 'NVIDIA kind of publicly endorsed Millennium early on' and 'we talked about the productivity of 50 to 60X', and that Cadence is now extending the platform from CFD to EDA solvers, naming Clarity (electromagnetic) and Celsius (thermal), with aerospace and defense and automotive as further targets.

connects_to.relationship: EDA tools, IP and agentic AI products supplied to Intel Foundry for the 14A node

contracts.signal: Gu: 'with Intel, we're doing a lot more, right? 14A, I think you probably noted that we signed a meaningful kind of deal with Intel to help them design their 14A on the foundry side. So it's not just IP, but also it helps with our EDA tools also and agent AI products.'
